correctness.rationale: For n=2^k p q, M=2^(k+1)-1 and a=M(p+1)-h q with h=p-M. In the strip p>M and p>h^2, h is even and at least two. The exact semiperfectness obstruction from Iannucci is equivalent to the nonexistence of a bounded representation a=r+s p+t q. When 0<a<q and a<Mp<pq, t must be zero, so weirdness is equivalent to a mod p>M. Reducing a modulo p gives a≡-h(q+1) mod p, so this is exactly h(q+1) mod p in {1,...,h-1}, equivalently q≡-1+u h^{-1} mod p. The strict abundance inequalities give M(p+1)/(h+1)<q<M(p+1)/h. These are both necessary and sufficient in the stated strip. The one-third-scale bound follows from q>M(p+1)/(h+1) and h>=2. For every proper divisor, the 2^j, 2^j p and 2^j q cases are deficient; for 2^j p q with j<k the abundance is U(1+p+q)-pq<0 because U=2^(j+1)-1<= (M-1)/2 and p,q>M. Thus the constructed weird numbers are primitive. The verifier source compares the exact interval predicate with direct divisor-subset sums for small k; finite tests are not used as the proof.
residual_risks: The proof depends on the exact bounded representation criterion as stated in Iannucci; that criterion and the algebraic reduction were checked against the full text.

value.rationale: The prime gap h=p-(2^(k+1)-1) defines a natural near-Mersenne regime tied to an open abundance bound. The result gives an exact congruence-and-interval classification for q and a stronger abundance bound in that strip, rather than a small numerical census or a restatement of the general criterion.
residual_risks: No infinitude assertion is made for the classified family; the theorem characterizes admissible q for each fixed k,p.

final_claim: For n=2^k p q with M=2^(k+1)-1, p=M+h, h>0, p>h^2 and q>p, weirdness is exactly the conjunction M(p+1)/(h+1)<q<M(p+1)/h and h(q+1) mod p in {1,...,h-1}; every such number is primitive and has abundance a<(M+1)(M+2)/3.
limitations: Only n=2^k p q with p<q odd primes and the explicit near-Mersenne strip p=M+h, p>h^2 is classified.
No infinitude assertion or universal one-third bound outside the strip is claimed.
